meta.notes: All figures are indicative and dated. Prices: Redfin statewide median sale price (all residential, Aug 2026). $/sqft mid: Redfin statewide average LIST $/sqft for most states (true median SALE $/sqft only for FL); low/high: Redfin median sale $/sqft of the cheapest / priciest major metro. Property tax: Tax Foundation effective rate on owner-occupied homes (2024 ACS, published Mar 2026); recent buyers in CA (Prop 13) and FL (Save Our Homes) pay more because assessments reset on sale. Insurance: NerdWallet 2026 state averages for a $400k dwelling; insurance_rate_pct = premium / $400,000. Sources diverge widely for FL, TX and CO insurance. Refresh the default rate weekly (Freddie Mac PMMS) and the conforming limits each November (FHFA).

pmi.notes: Annual PMI as % of the loan, estimated for a ~720–759 credit score (third-party compilations of 2026 insurer rate cards; Urban Institute range 0.46–1.50%). Real pricing depends on insurer, credit score, LTV and DTI. Cancellation: borrower may request at 80% of original value; automatic termination at 78% (Homeowners Protection Act).

mortgage_rules.notes: 28/36 is a planning guideline, not a legal limit. Fannie Mae (Selling Guide B3-6-02): max total DTI 36% for manually underwritten loans, up to 45% with credit-score and reserve requirements, 50% through Desktop Underwriter; no separate housing-ratio cap. The CFPB General QM rule removed the old 43% DTI cap (mandatory since 2022-10-01) and replaced it with a price-based test. 3% down: Fannie 97% LTV / HomeReady, Freddie Home Possible / HomeOne. Closing costs: LodeStar/Bankrate average ~1.6% excludes lender fees and prepaids; 3% all-in default with a 2–5% range. Maintenance: Fannie Mae homeowner guide, 1–4% of value per year (1% for newer homes). Fallback tax/insurance rates apply only when no state is chosen.

CA.name: California
CA.notes: Prop 13: a buyer's tax resets to about 1% of the purchase price plus local assessments (Mello-Roos), so the effective rate understates a new buyer's bill. Insurance market is stressed; wildfire areas cost far more than the average. High-cost conforming limits in coastal metros.

NY.name: New York
NY.notes: Property tax varies hugely (NYC much lower than the suburbs). NYC co-ops and condos add monthly charges; mansion tax applies at $1M+. High-cost conforming limits in the NYC metro.

TX.name: Texas
TX.notes: No state income tax, but high property tax (plus MUD/PID levies in new subdivisions); the homestead exemption lowers owner-occupant bills. Insurance among the most expensive in the US (hail, wind).

FL.name: Florida
FL.notes: Stressed insurance market: separate hurricane deductibles, flood insurance is separate, condo special assessments. Insurance sources disagree sharply (one 2026 source is more than double this average). Save Our Homes cap resets on sale. No state income tax.

WA.name: Washington
WA.notes: No state income tax on wages. Earthquake cover is excluded from standard policies. High-cost conforming limits in the Seattle metro.

MA.name: Massachusetts
MA.notes: Moderate effective tax rate; residential exemptions vary by town. Insurance below the national average but rising fast; coastal areas carry wind deductibles. High-cost conforming limits in the Boston metro.

CO.name: Colorado
CO.notes: Low property tax, but bills have been volatile after recent reassessments. Insurance expensive and rising (hail, Front Range wildfire). HOA and metro-district fees common in new builds.

IL.name: Illinois
IL.notes: Second-highest effective property tax in the US; often the biggest cost after the mortgage. Insurance above average (storms, hail). The $/sqft mid is an older listing snapshot (late 2025).

GA.name: Georgia
GA.notes: Moderate property tax with a statewide homestead assessment cap (unless a jurisdiction opted out). Insurance above average (storms; hurricane exposure on the coast). Prices flat to slightly down.
